scope: Design-level review checklist only. No compiler-specific circuit audit, proof forgery, or production exploit test was performed.
soundness_target: For the specified model, input encoding, and inference semantics, an accepted proof must imply that the public output satisfies the intended relation.

checklist.title: Range and representation constraints
checklist.review_question: For every bounded integer or quantized wire, does the circuit constrain the intended signed/unsigned range and its field-to-integer encoding?
checklist.potential_failure_if_unaddressed: If the intended range or encoding is not enforced, field elements may represent values outside the application's integer semantics. Whether that affects soundness depends on the actual circuit relation.
design_checks: Document the field-to-integer mapping, bit width, signedness, and overflow behavior.
Use backend-appropriate range-check or lookup constraints and test boundary values.
Inspect compiled constraints; a Python example is not evidence of a circuit exploit.

checklist.title: Tie-breaking and output semantics
checklist.review_question: If the public output is an index or ordered set, are ties and other boundary cases defined and is the circuit consistent with that definition?
checklist.potential_failure_if_unaddressed: Unspecified tie-breaking can make outputs implementation-dependent. Multiple valid internal witnesses alone do not imply unsoundness if the public output still satisfies the intended relation.
design_checks: Specify deterministic or set-valued semantics for ArgMax/TopK, including ties.
Constrain the public index/set to satisfy the selected semantics.
Test equal logits, near ties, and boundary values against a reference implementation.

checklist.title: Completeness of layer relations
checklist.review_question: Does the proof relation constrain every intermediate value needed to establish the prescribed model's input/output computation?
checklist.potential_failure_if_unaddressed: An omitted or weakly linked relation can permit witnesses that do not represent the intended graph; this is a review concern, not a finding about a specific backend.
design_checks: Trace each public output dependency through all required layers and residual paths.
Check that intermediate values are constrained by the intended layer relation.
Compare circuit outputs with a trusted reference on adversarial and boundary inputs.

checklist.title: Quantization configuration and semantics
checklist.review_question: Are scale, zero point, rounding, signedness, clipping, and overflow rules fixed to the authorized model/configuration and reflected in the circuit?
checklist.potential_failure_if_unaddressed: A mismatch between the intended and proved quantized function may change outputs; no such mismatch has been demonstrated here.
design_checks: Bind quantization parameters and configuration version to the authorized model.
Specify exact rounding, clipping, and overflow behavior.
Test the circuit against the same quantized reference implementation.

checklist.title: Model and version binding
checklist.review_question: Does the statement bind the weights and model version used by the circuit to the authorized model identifier or commitment?
checklist.potential_failure_if_unaddressed: If weights are supplied dynamically but not bound, a proof may concern a different model. If weights are fixed in the circuit, the circuit/version identifier still needs to be tied to the protocol's authorized model.
design_checks: Bind public or committed weights to the registered model/version.
If weights are private, constrain their commitment opening in the proof relation.
Test model-version changes and commitment mismatch cases.

illustrations.conclusion: Shows that an ordinary Python value can differ from a clamped example; it does not show that a ZK circuit accepts an out-of-range value.

rq2_answer: Five conditional design-review areas are listed for a future ZKML audit. They are not experimentally verified vulnerability classes or exploit findings.
